literal: Him who dwells upon words without benefit, calling a man [is wrong]; calling the chaff of people [is right].
translation: Do not call a person a man if he dwells upon useless words; call him the chaff among human beings.
modern: பயனில்லாத சொற்களைத் திரும்பத் திரும்பப் பேசுபவனை ஒரு மனிதன் என்று சொல்லக்கூடாது; அவனை மனிதர்களுள் பதர் என்றுதான் சொல்ல வேண்டும்.
explanation: The couplet strongly condemns the habit of speaking useless words. The word 'பாராட்டுவானை' refers to someone who repeatedly dwells upon or celebrates empty talk. The poet uses the word 'எனல்' (a verbal noun meaning saying or calling) twice to create a sharp contrast, functioning as an injunction. Calling such a person a 'மகன்' (a true human being) is wrong; instead, one should call him 'பதடி' (chaff), the empty husk of grain that has no substance or value among people.
